excerpts: Attackers Exploit Critical Siemens IoT2050 Flaw to Plant Remote Command Backdoors --> Attackers Exploit Critical Siemens IoT2050 Flaw to Plant Remote Command Backdoors  Ravie Lakshmanan  Nov 03, 2026 Vulnerability / Cyber Attack A maximum-severity security flaw impacting Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices has come under active exploitation, VulnCheck has revealed .

"SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices running Industrial OS with Node-RED installed contain a missing authentication vulnerability in the Node-RED HTTP interface that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to create malicious flows and execute arbitrary code on the underlying server with maximum privileges," Siemens said in an advisory released back in August 2026.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-58115 (CVSS score: 10.0), is a case of missing authentication for a critical function that could be exploited by an unauthenticated remote attacker to run arbitrary code.
This CVE was assigned by Siemens and affects the SIMATIC IoT2050 Advance, which shows the software is embedded in commercial ICS/OT products.
CVE-2026-58115 allows unauthenticated access to programming nodes that are capable of executing system commands on the server.

sources.name: BleepingComputer
excerpts: Administrators of affected Zyxel GS1900 switches are advised to install the latest firmware updates to protect against CVE-2026-107441.
The flaw affects ten GS1900 switch models, and Zyxel released security updates on October 22 and published a security advisory on November 3.
Attacks linked to zero-day flaw On June 16, 2026, Zyxel released security updates addressing CVE-2026-7273, a pre-authentication buffer overflow vulnerability affecting the same GS1900 switches.
However, the vulnerability was initially mistaken for an older flaw that Zyxel had already patched months before the attacks began.

Starting around August 17, cybersecurity company GreyNoise observed a suspected Chinese-speaking threat actor tracked as Kapibala exploiting Zyxel switches, reporting that the attackers compromised 996 devices across 48 countries.

The out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the CGI program of the Zyxel GS1900 series switch firmware could allow a LAN-based, unauthenticated attacker to exploit the flaw and potentially execute OS commands via a crafted HTTP request.

A stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the CGI program of the Zyxel GS1900 series switch firmware could allow a LAN-based, unauthenticated attacker to exploit the flaw and potentially execute OS commands via a crafted HTTP request.

excerpts: Some refrigeration systems were shut down entirely, while others had their temperature settings changed remotely.

The incident follows a wave of cyberattacks targeting refrigeration systems across Europe, where attackers remotely manipulate temperature settings or activate defrost functions that turn off cooling.
Belgian refrigeration company Sabcobel previously said that attackers behind the November incidents exploited the same vulnerability used in October's attacks against French supermarkets.

sources.name: The Register
excerpts: Ukraine's announcement of the alert app cyberattack came almost simultaneously with the official conclusion of a six-day ceasefire in Kherson.
"Citizens are alerted through primary channels: regional and municipal alert systems (sirens, loudspeakers), communication networks (SMS messaging), and television and radio broadcasts.

According to the messages sent to devices after the compromise of Ukraine's alert app, the fake warnings pertained to various threats, such as street fights in Kyiv, chemical attacks, and radiation hazards.
According to public statements and messages sent via social media, Ukraine’s alert app was hit first, with the country’s Air Force quick to dispel nuclear fears.

Stay calm, follow our messages on our channel!" REG AD At around 0030 UTC on Monday, Russia's Ministry of Emergency Situations confirmed the country’s app had also been abused, with fake messages sent to citizens' devices.
